newsitem.title: GERMANY: Viag, BT plan no cross-shareholdings.
newsitem.headline: Viag, BT plan no cross-shareholdings.

text.p: Viag chairman Georg Obermeier said on Thursday that Viag and British Telecom do not plan any cross-shareholdings when they merge their German telecommunications activities.
Responding to a reporter's question, Obermeier said: "Absolutely not. We are not thinking about cross-shareholdings. We don't consider this to be sensible."
Obermeier added that the companies would now quickly move to form a new joint company, but would give no details about the equity division, the name of the company, or its capital.
Viag and BT were hit on Wednesday by what Obermeier called the "abrupt" departure of electrical utility RWE AG from their telecoms alliance to link up instead with Veba AG and Cable & Wireless Plc.
BT and Viag are seeking new partners to join their efforts to crack the German telecoms market, over which Deutsche Telekom AG has a monopoly, after deregulation in 1998.
